title: Tenant fairshare throughput arbiter with rollback safety
creator: Priya Singh
description: Problem: Dedicated pools currently scale per-tenant using global heuristics that can starve lower-priority tenants during bursts and provide poor rollback behavior when a scaling decision causes regressions. This ticket proposes a tenant-aware fairshare arbiter that slices pool throughput across tenants according to configured SLAs and priorities, with an automated rollback safety mechanism that reverts problematic scale-ups quickly.
acceptance_criteria: New arbiter enforces per-tenant throughput allocation within +/- 10% of targets under steady-state traffic
Scaling decisions include a rollback token and can revert within 60s when regression signals exceed thresholds
No observable increase in 99th percentile token latency > 5% for unaffected tenants during canary rollout
Unit and integration tests for allocation logic, rollback triggers, and race conditions are in CI
design_notes: High level: implement an arbiter component in the Dedicated control-plane that seats between router and autoscaler. It computes per-tenant target capacity fractions and emits scaled requests to the autoscaler via the existing autoscale API.
Inputs: per-tenant SLA (throughput qps or tokens/sec), tenant priority, recent observed qps, backlog length, tail latency percentiles, and current pool capacity
Output: desired replica delta for the pool plus a bounded allocation map (tenant -> token share) used by packet/connection shapers in the serving runtime
Safety-first: decisions annotated with a rollback token and evaluation window. If rollback triggers fire, autoscaler must remove only the delta introduced by arbiter within a bounded time window
scaling_algorithm: Primary allocation: proportional fairshare computed as min(SLA_i, alpha * observed_demand_i) where alpha is a smoothing factor (default 1.2)
Headroom & burst handling: add burst buffer B = max(0, burst_factor * stddev(demand_window)) distributed proportionally to tenants with 'burst_enabled' flag
Scale command generation: translate aggregate desired throughput to replica delta using measured throughput_per_replica metric (EWMA over 60s), enforce max_step_up and max_step_down
Fallback controller: when predictive forecast fails (large demand variance), switch to conservative PID controller targeting 95th percentile latency instead of throughput

Rollback safety: emit scale actions as scoped transactions with an idempotent rollback id. Monitor rollback signals (error_budget_breach, latency_regression, dropped_requests) and perform automatic revert of last N deltas scoped to action id
metrics: Per-tenant backlog_length (requests queued waiting for capacity)
Tail latency percentiles (p95, p99) per tenant
Error rate (4xx/5xx) and dropped request count
safety_limits: max_step_up: 25% of current pool replicas (soft), with absolute cap of +10 replicas
max_step_down: 20% per minute with minimum replica floor enforced by SLA owners
cooldown_window: 120s after any scale-up before further step-ups unless emergency flag set
rollback_window: evaluate regressions for 60s post-decision; if triggers hit, revert delta within 30s
isolation_quota: reserve a small static headroom (default 5% of pool) for critical system traffic to avoid total exhaustion
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): route 5% of traffic/pools with 3 tenants to arbiter in read-only monitoring mode for 2 days
Phase 2 (shadow): apply decisions in shadow for 48 hours and compare against existing autoscaler metrics (no actual scale actions)
Phase 3 (pilot): enable for a single low-risk pool with automatic rollback enabled and tightened thresholds
Phase 4 (gradual): ramp to 25% pools, then 50% with checkout audits, then global if stable
Rollback playbook: documented steps plus automated API to manually revert individual scale transactions
test_plan: Unit tests: allocation math, burst distribution, rollback idempotency
Integration tests: end-to-end with autoscaler in staging pool using synthetic tenant traffic profiles (spike, ramp, diurnal)
Chaos tests: inject delayed replicas and faulty replicas while arbiter is active to validate rollback and safety-limits enforcement
Perf test: verify control-plane latency under 2000 concurrent tenants and ability to compute allocations in <100ms
Monitoring test: simulate regression signals and ensure rollback occurs and metrics emitted
observability: Dashboards: per-pool allocation heatmap, per-tenant SLA attainment, recent scale_transactions timeline
Traces: attach scale decisions to trace ids so we can correlate scale action -> increased latency/errors
Alerts: regression_alert (p99 increase > 20% post-scale), rollback_failed, allocation_violations
Audit logs: every arbiter decision persisted with inputs, outputs, and rollback id
risks: Incorrect allocation could cause SLA violations for high-priority tenants if weights misconfigured
Rollback may oscillate if signals are noisy; need smoothing and transient-tolerant thresholds
Increased control-plane load when computing allocations for thousands of tenants; must optimize compute path
Interaction with existing autoscaler cooldowns could lead to slower recovery unless coordinated
